hero.title: PageRank: Link Authority Mechanics
hero.subtitle: PageRank (Patent US6285999, Larry Page, 1998) models a random web surfer who clicks links with probability 0.85 and teleports randomly with probability 0.15. A page's PageRank equals the probability that this surfer lands on it. The modern system has evolved far beyond the original formula: the Reasonable Surfer model (US7716225) weights links by click probability, and PageRank_NS measures distance from trusted seed sites rather than raw link flow. The API leak revealed 7 active PageRank variants.

keyInsight.label: Key Insight from API Leak + DOJ Trial
keyInsight.text: The 2024 API leak revealed seven PageRank variants still active internally: pagerank, pagerank_ns, homepagePagerankNs, ToolbarPageRank, rawPagerank, pagerank2, and firstCoveragePagerank. The production version is PageRank_NS (Nearest Seed), which measures distance from trusted seed sites, not just link counting. HJ Kim confirmed PageRank feeds into Q* (Quality) as one of 'over 100 raw signals.' Pandu Nayak clarified: 'Most of Google's quality signal is derived from the webpage itself,' placing PageRank as important but not dominant. The original patent expired September 2019.

pillars.title: 4 Patents
items: Patent US6285999: Original PageRank (Larry Page, Stanford) - Random surfer model, damping factor 0.85, iterative eigenvector computation
Patent US7716225: Reasonable Surfer (Dean, Anderson, Battle) - Links weighted by click probability. Font size, position, color, context all affect weight
Patent US9165040: Seed-based distance ranking (Hajaj) - Shortest distances from diversified trusted seed pages, not raw link flow
Patent US8117209: Reasonable Surfer update - Enhanced user behavior and feature data for link weighting
Original patent expired Sept 2019. Assigned to Stanford (not Google). Stanford received 1.8M Google shares for exclusive license

pillars.title: API Leak: 7 PageRank Variants
items: pagerank: Base/classic PageRank score
pagerank_ns: PageRank-NearestSeeds (production version). Distance from trusted seed sites
homepagePagerankNs: Homepage-specific PageRank_NS. Trust anchor for all pages on domain
ToolbarPageRank: Legacy metric, no longer public since 2016, still computed internally
rawPagerank: Basic unmodified PageRank from pure link structure
pagerank2: Updated version (exact differences unknown)
firstCoveragePagerank: PageRank captured when Google first discovers a page
IndyRank: Backlink independence/diversity. Many unrelated sources > cluster of related sites

pillars.title: DOJ Trial Evidence
items: Pandu Nayak: PageRank is 'a single signal relating to distance from a known good source, used as input to Q*'
'Most of Google's quality signal is derived from the webpage itself' (PageRank important but not dominant)
HJ Kim: PageRank_NS feeds into NSR (Normalized Site Rank) computation
PageRank is one of 'over 100 raw signals' (Nayak testimony)
Q* (Quality) and P* (Popularity) are the two top-level ranking signals. PageRank contributes to Q*

HJ Kim (PXR0356, Feb 2025): Confirmed PageRank is 'a single signal relating to distance from a known good source,' used as 'an input to the Quality score.' Reinforces that PageRank is one component of Q*, not a standalone ranking factor

pillars.title: Reasonable Surfer: What Affects Link Value
items: Font size: Larger anchor text = higher click probability = more PageRank passed
Position: Links near top of page carry more weight. Footer/sidebar links devalued
Color/styling: Differently colored links, bold/italic styling affects perceived importance
Context: Words surrounding the anchor text affect link weight
Topical relevance: Anchor topic matching page topic increases weight
Click data: Actual user click frequency on a link affects its PageRank flow
Internal vs external: Same-domain links weighted differently from cross-domain
Outbound count: Fewer outbound links = more PageRank per link (dilution effect)

Yandex cross-reference: Yandex's FI_PAGE_RANK_BONUS applies dynamically to almost all 2+ word queries, giving links additional weight for less-frequent search terms. This suggests Google may similarly weight link authority differently by query length: for short head terms, brand/click signals dominate; for long-tail, links may matter more. Non-commercial link ratio is explicitly tracked in Yandex (confirming IndyRank's editorial independence concept)

calculations.name: Classic PageRank Formula
calculations.how: Each page's PageRank equals the probability that a random web surfer lands on it. With probability d (0.85), the surfer follows a random link. With probability (1-d), the surfer teleports to any random page. PageRank is computed iteratively until convergence, corresponding to the principal eigenvector of the normalized link matrix.
calculations.formula: PR(A) = (1-d)/N + d * ( PR(T1)/C(T1) + PR(T2)/C(T2) + ... + PR(Tn)/C(Tn) ) // d = 0.85 (damping factor) // C(Ti) = outbound links from page Ti // Iterative until convergence (eigenvector)
calculations.affects: Affected by: inbound link count, linking page quality, outbound link dilution, link graph structure

calculations.name: Reasonable Surfer Model
calculations.how: Replaces the random surfer (equal probability of clicking any link) with a reasonable surfer (varying probabilities based on link features). Links pass different amounts of PageRank based on the probability a real user would click them. Factors include font size, position, color, anchor text, context, topical relevance, and actual click data.
calculations.formula: LinkWeight(link) = P_click( font_size, position, color, anchor_text, context, topical_match, actual_clicks ) PR_passed = PR(source) * LinkWeight / sum(weights) // Not all links are equal
calculations.affects: Affected by: link prominence, position, styling, topical relevance, actual user click behavior

calculations.name: PageRank_NS (Nearest Seed)
calculations.how: The production PageRank variant. Instead of pure link-flow, measures shortest distance from diversified trusted seed pages to each page in the graph. Each topic/niche has its own seed set. Pages closer to seeds rank higher. This is NOT the same as TrustRank (which propagates trust like classic PageRank). This is a distance-based algorithm.
calculations.formula: PageRankNS(page) = min_distance( page, seed_set(topic) ) // Shorter distance = higher authority // Topic-specific seed sets (medical ≠ sports) // Feeds into Q* and NSR computation
calculations.affects: Affected by: link path to seed sites, seed set selection, link quality, topical alignment

stages.name: Link Graph Construction
stages.detail: Trawler crawls web, Alexandria builds link graph. Billions of pages, trillions of links

stages.name: Seed Selection
stages.detail: Diversified trusted seed sets selected per topic/niche (e.g., NYT, Wikipedia, .gov sites)

stages.name: Distance Computation
stages.detail: PageRank_NS computed as shortest distance from seeds, weighted by Reasonable Surfer link probabilities

stages.name: Homepage Propagation
stages.detail: homepagePagerankNs computed first. Acts as trust anchor for all pages on domain

stages.name: IndyRank Assessment
stages.detail: Backlink independence measured. Many unrelated sources > cluster of related sites

stages.name: Feed into Q*
stages.detail: PageRank_NS and related signals feed into Q* (Quality score) alongside content and spam signals

timeline.title: Original PageRank
timeline.desc: Larry Page files US6285999 at Stanford. Random surfer model with d=0.85 damping factor.

timeline.title: Reasonable Surfer
timeline.desc: US7716225 filed. Links weighted by click probability. Font size, position, context all matter.

timeline.title: Seed-Based Distance
timeline.desc: US9165040 filed. PageRank_NS measures distance from trusted seeds, not raw link flow.

timeline.title: Toolbar PageRank Hidden
timeline.desc: ToolbarPageRank removed from public view. Still computed internally.

timeline.title: Patent Expires
timeline.desc: Original PageRank patent (US6285999) expires September 2019. Algorithm continues internally.

timeline.title: Yandex Leak Cross-Reference
timeline.desc: Yandex leak confirms active PageRank with BM25 for anchor+body relevance (not TF*IDF). FI_LINK_RELEV evaluates link relevance per-query (dynamic, not static). FI_PAGE_RANK_BONUS applies extra link authority weight for 2+ word queries, suggesting link importance is query-length dependent. Homepage links weighted higher than deep page links. Top-100 PageRank sites carry disproportionate weight. Wikipedia links confirmed as a strong quality signal.

timeline.title: 7 Variants Revealed
timeline.desc: API leak reveals 7 active PageRank variants: pagerank, pagerank_ns, homepage, toolbar, raw, v2, firstCoverage.

timeline.title: DOJ: Input to Q*
timeline.desc: Nayak confirms PageRank is 'a single signal' feeding into Q*. One of 'over 100 raw signals.'

timeline.title: HJ Kim Confirms Distance-Based Definition (PXR0356)
timeline.desc: HJ Kim (DOJ Remedies Exhibit PXR0356, Feb 2025): PageRank is 'a single signal relating to distance from a known good source,' used as 'an input to the Quality score.' Confirms PageRank_NS (distance from seeds) is the production variant.

contradictions.publicClaim: PageRank is just one of many signals. We no longer publish Toolbar PageRank. Links are less important than they used to be.
contradictions.internalSource: API Leak: 7 active PageRank variants + Q* integration
contradictions.internalClaim: The API leak revealed seven PageRank variants still active: pagerank, pagerank_ns, homepagePagerankNs, ToolbarPageRank, rawPagerank, pagerank2, firstCoveragePagerank. PageRank feeds into Q* (Quality), a top-level Ascorer pillar. Google stopped publishing the Toolbar version but never stopped computing or using PageRank internally. Seven active variants suggests PageRank remains deeply integrated into ranking.

contradictions.publicSource: Google (public emphasis on content quality over links)
contradictions.publicClaim: Focus on creating great content. Links will come naturally. Content quality matters more than link building.
contradictions.internalSource: DOJ: T* = Anchors + Body + Clicks + PageRank feeds Q*
contradictions.internalClaim: PageRank feeds Q* (quality pillar). Anchor text is one-third of T* (topicality pillar). Links affect TWO of the three top-level Ascorer pillars. The Reasonable Surfer model (US7716225) evolved PageRank to weight links by click probability, making link quality more important than ever. Content quality alone affects Body (one-third of T*) and some Q* sub-signals, but links influence a broader portion of the scoring function.
